text: Obeying the Law of the Lord is the same as bringing him many gifts,
and obeying his commands is like offering a sacrifice to ask his blessing.[78]
Showing kindness to someone who has been kind to you is like offering a sacrifice to give thanks to the Lord.[79]
And giving to the poor is offering a sacrifice that gives the Lord praise.
So please the Lord and seek his forgiveness, by staying away from evil.
However, do not come to worship the Lord without bringing him a gift
as his Law commands.
When one of God's people burns the fat of a sacrifice, God Most High is pleased with the smell of the smoke rising from the altar.
Such sacrifices are acceptable to God and will not be forgotten.
When you offer to the Lord the first part of the harvest or a sacrifice to give thanks, be generous—not stingy.
Be happy and cheerful when you give him a gift or a tenth of your harvest.
Be as generous with the Lord as he has been with you.
Remember! The Lord is the one who repays seven times more than you give him.
You cannot bribe the Lord by offering a sacrifice,
and he won't accept as a gift what you get by cheating. The Lord is a judge who doesn't take sides,
especially against the poor, but he answers the prayers of all who suffer injustice.
God listens when an orphan begs for his help. He hears the complaints of a mistreated widow as she cries out
with tears in her eyes
and tells him about the one who has abused her.
If you obey the Lord, he will accept you and answer when you pray.
Be humble, and your prayers will go up beyond the clouds and be heard by God Most High.
He will quickly punish those who have wronged his people and completely crush those who have shown no mercy.
God will take revenge on evil, arrogant Gentiles,[80] breaking their power and destroying them.
And someday, all humans will be repaid, as their thoughts and deeds deserve.
Then God will judge in favor of his people, and they will celebrate because he showed mercy.
We welcome God's mercy when we are in trouble, just as we welcome rain in hot, dry weather.
